material_definitions: In order to better understand the effect of aliovalent doping in Li+ conducting argyrodites, the substitution of P5+ with Si4+ was performed in the solid solutions Li(6+x)P(1-x)SixS5X.
By combining structural characterizations, i.e. X-ray and neutron diffraction with electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, we show the effect of increasing the Si4+ content on the ionic conductivity.
The study investigates aliovalent substituted argyrodite superionic conductors with the general formula Li(6+x)P(1-x)SixS5Br, where increasing x corresponds to higher Si4+ and Li+ content.
Ionic conductivity was assessed via temperature-dependent impedance spectroscopy.
The room-temperature ionic conductivity of the unsubstituted sample (x=0) was 0.7 mS cm-1.
The highest conductivity was observed for x = 0.35, reaching 2.4 mS cm-1.
